leads.summary: On the current base the screenshot picker bypasses this fix, and Omasnap still lists covered clients
leads.consequence: Fresh installs and upgraded installs launch Omasnap for Print Screen, the menu Screenshot action and `omarchy capture screenshot windows`; Omasnap builds its own window list from hyprctl JSON without inspecting visible or hidden, so covered fullscreen/maximized siblings can still be offered for screenshot picking. The changed helper still affects the screenrecording picker and direct invocations, but no longer fixes screenshots. Integrate the same visibility predicate into Omasnap's window discovery (coordinated upstream), or narrow the claim to recorder/direct legacy picker and test both routes against the current base.
leads.triage: already in Opus final; corroboration. Omasnap behaviour settled further via Opus follow-up (opus/followup-omasnap.md)

leads.summary: Open #11441 conflicts in window_rects, and its new multi-display fixture fails if both filters are kept
leads.consequence: The two diverged PRs both replace window_rects(); a three-way merge of their heads using #11441's parent yields conflict markers rather than a working merged file. Resolving by retaining both changes (all active workspaces and visible==true) makes #11441's current fixture see zero windows, because its JSON clients omit visible; the fixture exits 1 before later assertions, blocking the combined test suite. Retain both intended filters when resolving and add visible:true to the fixture's intended selectable clients, visible:false for its hidden client. The default screenshot route now uses Omasnap, so this combined helper fix applies to recorder/direct picker only, not Omasnap.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #11441 diff (same filter line, fixture lacks visible); Opus plan3 run confirmed

leads.summary: Open #12252 merges textually, but its snap-to-window regression fixture has no visible field
leads.consequence: With both independent PRs combined, `window_rects()` correctly rejects missing visible on the synthetic clients, so a bare click on the floating window instead snaps to the full monitor. #12252's test exits 1 and breaks the combined suite even though its real Hyprland clients always have a boolean visible. Add visible:true to both synthetic windows, retaining this PR's exclusion of false siblings.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #12252 fixture lacks visible; Opus plan3 run confirmed

leads.summary: New regression fixture misses the default smart and keyboard paths, allowing mode-dependent exclusion to regress
leads.consequence: The test calls only `omarchy-capture-region windows`; a plausible implementation that applies visible filtering only in `windows` while retaining hidden filtering for `smart` and `--select-window` passes every new assertion yet leaves covered siblings in screen recording's default smart picker and navigation. Add a smart-mode slurp-input assertion and exercise keyboard selection with a stubbed slurp process/pgrp rather than assuming shared code is always reused.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus plan3 confirmed smart-gated mutant passes PR test and smart-mode assertion catches it

flags.claim: Covered-sibling behaviour still holds in omarchy-capture-region '(all picker modes)'
flags.why: Only the modes that use window_rects() are affected: windows, smart, --take-window, --select-window. region mode runs slurp with no rectangles and fullscreen mode has no picker.
flags.disposition: real error (all picker modes too broad): fixed, listed modes

flags.claim: Merged onto that base, the changed filter reaches only screen recording (also L19-24 diagram and L40 'the remaining production caller')
flags.why: The slurp key binds in utilities.lua fire on any layer with namespace 'selection', and slurp 1.5.0 always uses that namespace. omarchy-capture-text (OCR) and omarchy-capture-qr run plain slurp, so Tab/Ctrl+Tab/arrows during an OCR or QR selection run 'omarchy-capture-region --select-window', which builds candidates from window_rects() and warps the cursor. The effect is small (which window centres the cursor jumps between in a freeform picker) and was not run.
flags.disposition: real overstatement (only screen recording): fixed to 'mainly' plus OCR/QR key-bind warp in Impact and 'main remaining caller'

flags.claim: Keyboard: Super+Arrow can move to a covered sibling, and Enter captures it.
flags.why: Enter runs chooseWindow(), which sets the selection to the covered window's old rectangle. Omasnap captures the monitor before its overlay appears, so the result shows the maximized window's pixels in that rectangle, not the covered window. 'captures it' can read as capturing the hidden window's content. The mode qualifier is also missing here: on 1.20.1 this works only in windows mode. L32 covers the 1.20.1 default.

flags.claim: Hover and click pick the covered window only when it comes after the maximized one in Hyprland's client list.
flags.why: This is exact for tiled siblings and true fullscreen, where every covered rectangle lies inside the maximized or fullscreen one. For a maximized (work-area) window, a covered floating window that extends outside the work area, for example over the bar, can be hovered in that outside part in any order: windowAt checks containment only, and the covered window is dropped only by alpha. This is a rare edge case, source only.
flags.disposition: nitpick (floating overhang outside work area): left

flags.claim: On 1.20.1 ... there only `omarchy capture screenshot windows` is affected.
flags.why: The singular 'window' also selects Window mode, and the wrapper passes unknown arguments through, so Omasnap's --capture-window/--capture-windows option does too. The substance is right: plain `omarchy screenshot` and `smart` map to Region.

flags.claim: With `.visible == true`, such clients are dropped (only the monitor rectangle is offered).
flags.why: 'Such clients are dropped' is verified for both PRs. The parenthetical fits #12252 (its first assertion then gets `actual: 0,0 2560x1440`). It does not fit #11441: that test calls window_rects() directly, which returns nothing, and #11441's monitor_rects() offers every enabled display, which is two in its fixture.
flags.disposition: real error for #11441: fixed to 'window assertions fail'

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier automated review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12512#issuecomment-5828075664), checked at head `34d3befe`. **Verified:** the only change since the reviewed head `9b90a878` is the test's failure message, which resolves the earlier optional test note. The `window_rects()` change is identical, and the earlier verified points still hold for `omarchy-capture-region`. **New:** on the current `quattro` base, screenshots no longer go through `omarchy-capture-region`, so this PR no longer reaches the screenshot picker that issue #8275 reports.

| Earlier point | Status at `34d3befe` |
|---|---|
| Covered siblings of a maximized or fullscreen window are dropped; visible, pinned and raised floating windows are kept | Still holds in `omarchy-capture-region` (`windows` and `smart` modes, `--take-window`, `--select-window`). Its reach changed, see below |
| `visible` key present from Hyprland 0.55.0, the release that added the Lua config and `hyprctl eval` | Still holds |
| Scope note: `visible` is alpha-based, not geometric; brief `visible: true` during the fade | Unchanged |
| Optional test improvement: literal `\n` in the failure message | Resolved: failures now print real line breaks |

### Screenshots on the current base use Omasnap, not this picker

Base PR #9446 moved screenshots to Omasnap. On `quattro` at `c3e67f5d`, `bin/omarchy-capture-screenshot` ends with `exec omasnap "${omasnap_args[@]}"`. Merged onto that base, the changed filter mainly reaches screen recording:

```text
Print key / menu Screenshot / omarchy screenshot / omarchy capture screenshot windows
  -> omarchy-capture-screenshot -> omasnap                              not changed by this PR
Screen recording
  -> omarchy-capture-screenrecording:141
     -> omarchy-capture-region smart --match-monitor -> window_rects()  fixed by this PR
```

Omasnap's picker was read at source only (1.20.1 on the stable and rc channels, 1.21.0 on edge). `parseWindows` keeps every client on the focused workspace and checks neither `hidden` nor `visible`. By that reading, covered siblings can still be reached for #8275's steps:

- **Keyboard:** Super+Arrow can move to a covered sibling, and Enter selects its old rectangle.
- **Outlines:** `windows` mode draws outlines for covered siblings too.
- **Hover and click:** these pick the covered window only when it comes after the maximized one in Hyprland's client list. Maximizing does not reorder that list.

On 1.20.1, plain `omarchy screenshot` opens Region mode, so there only Window mode (for example `omarchy capture screenshot windows`) is affected. None of this was run in a live session.

**Impact:** after merge, the fix applies to the screen-recording picker, plus the Tab and arrow-key window warp that the slurp key binds also run during OCR and QR selection. `quattro` is the default branch, so `Fixes #8275` would auto-close an issue whose reported commands go through Omasnap and likely still reproduce.

**Suggested change:** describe the PR as a fix for the screen-recording picker and replace `Fixes #8275` with a non-closing reference such as `Refs #8275`. The screenshot side needs the same `visible == true` filter in Omasnap's window discovery (`parseWindows` in `src/capture.cpp`).

**Related open PRs:** #11441 rewrites the same `window_rects()` filter line. The synthetic clients in #11441's `capture-multiple-displays-test.sh` and in #12252's `capture-region-test.sh` have no `visible` key. With `.visible == true`, such clients are dropped, so those tests' window assertions fail. Whichever of these PRs lands second needs `visible: true` on the selectable fixture clients, and #11441 and this PR also need their two filter predicates combined.

**Optional test improvement:** all three assertions run `omarchy-capture-region windows`, but screen recording, the main remaining production caller, uses `smart --match-monitor`. A variant that applies the old `hidden` filter only in `smart` mode still passes every assertion. A `smart`-mode assertion on the maximized case would cover the path that ships.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `34d3befe` against the earlier reviewed head and the PR base `c3e67f5d`. Later `quattro` commits up to `bf44355a` do not touch the capture scripts. The PR's test was run in an isolated sandbox on the merged tree (pass) and against the unpatched base (fails at the maximized case), directly and through the base's `test/shell` runner. The related PRs' tests were also run against this PR's filter. Synthetic `hyprctl` JSON scenarios covered `windows` and `smart` modes, `--take-window` and `--select-window`, with stubbed `hyprctl`, `slurp` and `hyprpicker`. Omasnap's picker and Hyprland 0.56.2 client ordering were assessed by source only. There was no live Hyprland session, so real picker behavior, fade timing and Omasnap were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
